back: Evaporation from the soil plus transpiration from plants: the total water lost as vapour from a field.
Temporary: recovers when water loss falls. Permanent: soil at the permanent wilting point; no recovery without water.

front: When and where does frost form?
back: On clear, calm winter nights, mainly in low-lying hollows where cold air collects.
Avoid hollows, time planting, irrigate the day before, cover or mulch, grow frost-tolerant crops.
The share of rain that enters the soil and is available to plants after runoff and evaporation.
How much rainfall amount and timing vary between seasons; low where rainfall is low.
Amount of rain per unit time (e.g. mm per hour); high intensity causes runoff and erosion.
Pollen and seed spread, more transpiration, lodging, spread of pests and diseases, wind erosion.
Less transpiration, more fungal disease; worse heat stress in livestock.
Roughly November to March (one season); dry season about April to October.
